Thank you for seeing me. You mentioned shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; can you tell me exactly when the pain started and if it happens on the left or right side?

REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor

The pain is localized to the right ear and occurs without systemic symptoms like fever; do you notice any fluid or discharge coming from that ear, and can you move your jaw without triggering a sharp increase in pain?

REQUEST TEST: Audiometry

speaker: Doctor
text:
The audiometry and otoscopy results are normal, which helps rule out simple fluid buildup or acute infection; do you feel any crunching or clicking in your right ear when you move your jaw or swallow?

REQUEST TEST: Microscopic Exam of Canal and Tympanic Membrane

speaker: Doctor
text:
The microscopic exam confirmed the tympanic membrane is intact with no granulation tissue or cholesteatoma; do you experience a distinct crunching sensation or a feeling of fullness when you chew or swallow?

REQUEST IMAGES: Post-tympanoplasty CT Temporal Bone

The imaging shows no bony erosion or cholesteatoma, ruling out structural complications from your surgery; does the shooting pain radiate to your upper teeth or scalp, and do you experience a severe stabbing sensation when you brush your hair or touch the skin over your ear?

REQUEST TEST: Valsalva Maneuver

speaker: Doctor
text:
The Valsalva maneuver was normal, and you deny pain radiating to the teeth or scalp upon touch; given your history of tympanoplasty, do you notice any specific triggers like wind entering the ear canal or sudden changes in pressure?

REQUEST TEST: Cold Threshold Test for the Trigeminal Nerve

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the normal audiometry, imaging, and Valsalva maneuver, combined with your history of tympanoplasty and the difficulty wearing earrings, do you notice any numbness, tingling, or a "pins and needles" sensation in the skin of your right ear or the side of your face?

REQUEST TEST: Trigeminal Nerve Sensory Examination
REQUEST IMAGES: High-resolution CT Temporal Bone focusing on the Foramen of Huschke and mastoid air cells

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-tympanoplasty Trigeminal Neuralgia (likely involving the Auriculotemporal nerve or a residual Foramen of Huschke defect causing neuropathic pain).
